mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES over the next month will increase commute-linked footfall to malls, dining, and service retail, lifting RETAIL_REC relative to the prior four weeks. The effect should appear within 4 weeks if mobility restrictions do not tighten again.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise over the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior four-week mean, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates more time spent at home, which suppresses discretionary shopping trips and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks. This signal is strongest when RESIDENTIAL stays above its recent weekly mean.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 6 points for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated for two weeks but RETAIL_REC rises versus the prior two-week average, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed decline in TRANSIT combined with weak WORKPLACES mobility indicates tighter movement constraints, which will reduce in-person shopping and lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if transit falls without any workplace contraction.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -10 points and WORKPLACES stays below -15 points
failure_condition: If TRANSIT drops below -10 and WORKPLACES remains below -15 for a week but RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next month, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: An improvement in GROCERY_PHARM reflects more routine out-of-home errands and higher neighborhood circulation, which should spill over into retail visits and raise RETAIL_REC within one week. The effect is expected to be short-lived and visible first in convenience-linked retail.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM increases week-on-week but RETAIL_REC is flat or lower in the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in PARKS mobility relative to the recent baseline signals outdoor leisure demand and broader weekend activity, which will translate into more incidental retail visits over the next four weeks. The mechanism is strongest when park use rises while commuting remains stable.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -15 points while TRANSIT is not falling
failure_condition: If PARKS improves without a subsequent increase in RETAIL_REC over the next month, or if TRANSIT drops sharply instead of holding steady, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises sharply while WORKPLACES remain depressed, people are substituting toward staying home and away from discretionary shopping, which will reduce RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The signal is a homebound-demand regime rather than a commuting regime.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 8 points and WORKPLACES below -20 points
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 8 while WORKPLACES stays below -20 but RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in TRANSIT from negative territory toward the baseline indicates eased access to city centers, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. This mechanism requires transit to improve without a simultaneous new drop in WORKPLACES.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses from below -5 to above -5
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses above -5 and remains there but RETAIL_REC does not outperform its previous four-week mean, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated while PARKS also recover, the combined pattern indicates broad local movement and errands that should spill into retail purchases over the next one to two weeks. The effect fails when grocery activity rises only because people substitute essentials for discretionary spending.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above 25 points and PARKS above -20 points
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both remain above the stated thresholds but RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.
